segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I’m glad you came back to talk again, Bob. I told you the reason why we’re doing this, but you can tell me your full name in English again.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Oh OK… OK, my name is Bob Dean Pettit.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How about in Cherokee?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: And my Cherokee name they call me Di-gu-te-s-ga. That’s it. I used to have a cousin, his name was Tsu-da-e-ga. He was Tsu-da-e-ga and I’m Di-gu-te-s-ga.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Who named you?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: That I know and remember. Do you remember Bill? Bill Pettit and Cindy?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: They used to call me that all the time as I grew up.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They’re Billy George’s parents.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, they are Billy George’s parents. Yeah, that’s what they named me.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Tell me again where you grew up.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: I’ll start with when me and Michael wrestled around when he was a little boy.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Where was that?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Right there where Wa-ne used to live. Down the holler at the end, there’s a mountain. Just right there on top. We used to hunt raccoons there. We used to hang out all the time when we were just young boys. His name is Michael Cooksey in English. And that Arch Flute, one of his young boys is named Archie, another one is named Tommy, and another one is named Bob Waters. We were all together one year. Michael and Bob’s mothers were sisters. We were up there on top [of the mountain]. We built a fire. We had already walked around a long way. The dogs we had weren’t finding any raccoons. We were out there quiet, sitting around, and me and Bob, Bob Waters, we were already grown-ups. Them boys wanted to wrestle so we got after it out there in the woods on the mountain. We wrestled for a long time there. And the late Bob was telling them, “Don’t do that, boys. Y’all can’t do that to old men.” We just quit right then. I don’t know if we all got tired. We had a spot that big [gesture], it was clear.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Where y’all wrestled?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Where we wrestled, yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: That’s what we were talking about a while ago. Back then, whichever way you went in the woods, when you thought, “I’m going whichever way,” you would go that way, ain’t it? Nowadays, you can’t even go stand over there. That’s how much it’s changed, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s how much it’s changed. It’s those rich people. They are in the way. They’re beating us. Just like when they put the fence up by my house. It didn’t even belong to the guy who put it there, and that lot where Sauce used to live, it don’t belong to him either. He said, “Too many people are chasing my deer and ducks away, shooting around.” I don’t know if he went by that. I’ve never seen an Indian with a gun there that I know of. I’ve seen White people shooting around there. I’ll tell them the truth if we talk in person.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Cherokees mostly fish there, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, they used to, but nobody’s fishing there anymore.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: So he locked it?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: He locked it. He’s got a cable up.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Something else changed. When you said y’all wrestled, y’all were just having fun without anybody getting mad.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, nobody getting mad.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Nowadays, somebody’s going to get mad.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Somebody will get mad real quick. It wasn’t like that back then. And then again, further back, you know we would box, and it was just for fun, too. And it was nothing wrong. That’s how it was for us Cherokees. Where we went, there was no getting mad. It’s like what you’re saying, I know it. Nobody was getting mad at anyone. Now, a person will get mad by just a word. They’ll get mad just by saying a word.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Or if they look at you different.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, or just that. Just over nothing, they’ll start trouble. It’s gotten worse. What you were saying, Michael, back when we were growing up, I had a lot of pigs. I still have a few pigs but I’m not able to buy them feed. I just have a few. I have a wild one penned up. I tamed it. There’s a few of them, but when I decided to pen them up – when I thought I was going to pen them up, they all left. Only one stayed, and I penned that one up. There was one really big one, a mean and scary-looking one. I’ve never seen one like it – and its teeth.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Was it the long-headed one?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, kind of like that one.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: They’re kind of rounded on the rump side, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: That’s the kind I have penned up. It probably weighs over 200 pounds, and it’s a boar. Yeah, I got that kind penned up. People ask me, “How did you get it in there?” The White people we were talking to. When a wild pig charges at you… “I grew up herding pigs and watching what they are doing, and I know what they are thinking, too,” I said. I said, “When I watch them in that cattle pen where they keep the cows penned up, that’s the kind of fence I have up where I have the pigs penned up.” They said, “Did you catch it and throw it over, or did you just put it in there?” I told them, “No, it was a wild one.” They asked me, “How did you do that?” “It’s like what I’m telling y’all. I knew when it was going to charge me. I got ready when it ran towards me. A wild pig won’t get you right here [gesture]. It’s going to bump into you here somewhere [gesture]. A wild pig won’t do what a regular pig will do. It’s going to charge you at your chest, and when it done that, when it came up, I went down,” I told them. “I caught it in the air and threw it over.” They said, “You sure did learn some amazing stuff!” I told them, “I sure did – amazing.” Yeah, back then, what I’m telling right now, where we were wrestling, there’s another valley and a mountain there. Back when the government passed the law that you had to pen up animals, boys, I had 600 pigs then. People were saying I had the most pigs then. Right there where Wa-ne used to live, down the holler, back then, cows, horses, pigs, and pets… they were branding horses and cows, and for pigs, they were doing something to their ears. Then people that lived close by knew who it belonged to. That’s what we did to them, and them pigs were taking off… Boys, when I was nine years old, where the late Do-ya/Beaver used to live, starting from where the spring is on this side of Bunch, I went all the way along there looking for pigs. I went all the way to where they call Brushy. When I was nine years old, starting from Highway 51 and Bunch and them mountains, I had already been all over when I was nine years old, by myself. That’s how I grew up. And all the pigs that I looked for, I brought them back in the fall. When they had piglets, it was hard to do something with them. Finally, I figured out a way. I thought, “If I catch a baby one and it squeals, the adult might go after it.” So that’s what I did, and that’s what happened. The adult chased me a ways, and when I turned around, it would be standing there, and I’d make the piglet squeal again. That’s how I brought them back with the piglets, ’cause it was hard to herd them piglets. And then later on, do y’all remember Ga-s-go-yu? The late Ga-s-go-yu Do-ya?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Hubert?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah. Right there where the holler is, De-wi No-k-s used to live where the holler is. Right there was a turnoff by De-wi, and on this side there was a wooden house. That’s where Ga-s-go-yu lived. Later on, my dad told me, “Son, I talked to Ga-s-go-yu. He said he has a dog that he’ll give you if you want it.” I was happy. It was the kind they call Redbone. I said, “When can we go get it?” That was when Ga-s-go-yu chased coyotes and foxes and he had dogs. Dad said, “He’s not doing anything. He’s got something treed – I don’t know what it is.” I told him, “Boy, let’s go get it.” And we went to get it. That was when I had some dogs the late K-l-s-to gave me. He gave me little ones.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Arthur Springwater?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Black and tan. I raised those. They got real good at hunting squirrels. I had another one that was brown. Me and my brothers were hunting, and we had that Redbone with us, and when they treed a squirrel or raccoon, that Redbone would lay down somewhere. There was nothing I’ve ever heard of – I had a dog and I didn’t know if it ever barked. This is what happened, boys, whenever they passed a law that you had to pen up pigs or cows or horses and pets. They were living that way. There were seven castrated ones. They were real big and I couldn’t bring them back. They weighed about 400 pounds. It was towards fall, right there on top where Su-s-hna used to live, they were just turning back around, right there back towards the spring. Then behind them, I tried to round them up. I always had it with me. It always followed me around, that Redbone. And right there, gaw, boys, it was making me cry, what them pigs were doing to me. I just sat on the ground and got me a stick. I was sitting there sticking that stick in the ground. I was thinking, “Where did them pigs run off to?” And my partner was just sitting beside me, staring at me. I told him, “Turn around, or I’m going to poke you in the head with this stick.” After a while, he was sitting there and I looked at him. He just looked up and started crying. It was real warm, too. It was towards the end of September. I got up real fast. I looked for a tree that I could climb, and I saw one. I took off and ran towards it. I thought that dog went crazy. It started hollering right quick. I climbed that tree. I was up in it, and the dog kept walking around, and I was watching it. Long time ago, when I was growing up, a lot of dogs went crazy. Not just dogs – a lot of different things were going crazy. That’s why I thought that, so I called it by its name. I called it Red. I said, “Red, do you feel OK?” He was just standing there, looking at me. I said, “Red, do you feel OK?”

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: What if he said, “What about you?”

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: That would have been towards the house. Finally, I jumped down. I thought, “I guess he’s OK, nothing wrong with him.” Then he started looking around, just looking. I thought, “Boy, he’s thinking about those pigs,” and then I knew which way the pigs went. I took him that way. The leaves were up. I told him, “Right here, Red,” I told him, “they went this way.” That dog took off fast. Maybe 100 feet or a little more, he barked big and he barked long. That’s the first time I heard that dog bark, and I’d had him for about three years. He was hollering. He went down towards the spring, and I was standing there listening to which way he turned them. I ran to Yu-tsi/Cave Spring School, then I ran to that other mountain where we were wrestling. He was hollering at about the middle of Yu-tsi/Cave Spring School by the creek. The dog was hollering and I still came down. I came across where we were wrestling. When I got there, that well where we got water from, just right by it, I used roots to make it soft and a shovel. I made it pretty good sized, and I got water from the well and poured it in there for the pigs to swim. And when I stopped, right there where the cemetery is, that’s where he was chasing them pigs. But I was still over here. I took off running down the hill. I got there and ran that way [gesture]. I thought them pigs might go there. They were sticking out of the water and mud, the red dog was latched on to a pig’s hind leg, and he was laying beside the pig.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: He made him stay there?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, he laid that big pig down right there. And the next morning, I went to look for the pigs, we penned these up. I had a little fence up, and we put them in there. That’s what happened to that dog. All I had to do was point at it and say, “Right here.”

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Bobby, did y’all live in that holler by the cemetery? Were there a lot of houses?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, there were a lot of houses.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: How many houses were there?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: One, two, three, four – there were four houses there, and then where Wa-ne used to live, one, two – there were two houses. Your uncle Joe used to live there, and then another one beside there where that cattle guard goes across, that’s when you keep going. And here it’s like this. That’s where Joe used to live.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Where Wa-ne used to live? Is that where Jim lives now? Is that where you’re talking about?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, where Jim lives.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: So, there were a lot of houses there?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, there were a lot of houses there back then.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: How about where they used to throw junk, on top of the mountain? Were there any houses there a long time ago?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: On this side, where the water was coming out, right there. Do y’all remember Di-gu-tla-da?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: No.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: No, I don’t.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: My grandpa’s brother, Wa-ha-ya his name was, Tom Pettit, that’s where he used to live, where you’re saying. There used to be houses right there. Right there, boys. I was just little. I was maybe six years old when Di-gu-tla-da used to live there. That’s where my dad was telling me he found rattlesnakes somewhere, this big [gesture]. Year after year, the rattlesnakes lived with that old man there. My dad said the last time he saw them, they were this big [gesture]. One of them, when you got to his house, it would be curled up there in the doorway, and another one would be curled up by his bed.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: I’ve heard of that before, a long time ago. Somebody would say, “Boy, he had some snakes, ain’t it?” Have you heard of that?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: That’s what he’s saying.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: There used to be some snake callers a long time ago. Somebody was saying that right there at Tsu-da-wa-di-s-ga Marble (Evening Shade Marble). When you come to Marble, then go towards Tsu-da-wa-di-s-ga (Evening Shade), and go over it, just on the right side there. He told me there used to be big ones there. And there was this one, he lived in Chewey somewhere, he was a snake caller. He went to visit them over there in Marble. He was saying, “I call snakes,” and showed the people that the snakes can really come when you call them. He said, “If you know where snakes are living,” he said, “that’s where I knew,” he said. “Take me there.” He said, “There’s a big square rock, but it’s a long one,” he said. “It’s probably 30 feet long,” he said. “You can step on it real good, and there’s a little tree next to it, and that i-tla-yo/tall grass is growing there on the bluff.” He told me to wait right there. He said, “I’m going to show you some snakes in a few minutes.” I thought, “I think he really means it.” He said, “I looked at that tree and said I’m just going to stand right here and I climbed it. I was standing there,” he said. He was standing way over there. After a while, on this side of the rock where I was, I saw that grass going like this [gesture], and the wind wasn’t even blowing. He said, “I was staring at it.” A rattlesnake went by. He was measuring it, being this big [gesture]. He said it was about 20 feet long. He said, “When that one went by, I was watching it. It went on by.” I did this and looked at the old man. There was a big snake above his head, behind him. I said, “Old man, there’s one standing behind you.” He turned around and hollered once, and made noise on the cliff. He said I was scared to get down. He said I’m going to have to get down. He said I finally got down and when I got there, he was sitting inside, and them locked out. Boy, I laughed out loud. That old man would take off.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: I miss those that were alive long time ago when I was little. Wi-li-s-an Di-ga-a-l-s-ga A-ma-ga-s-ga like Sambo. They would be walking somewhere, doing something.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, doing something.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Uh, Bob, you were telling me one time a big snake came to your house. Do you remember that?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Oh, yeah, that one that almost got me?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah, tell us about that one.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: I think I lost most of my blood veins then. That’s when I became shaky. Right there, where we have a water hydrant you say in English, I had some tomatoes planted there. Boy, there was some pretty ones on there. There were some little ones on three branches, but they weren’t turning out good. Those tomatoes were just white. I thought they might just need some soil. And just on this side where they threw junk away, I looked over there. I gave them water and plowed them tomatoes. There was an old coffee can there, and I thought I could use that. Boys, I was probably there 15-20 minutes and this was where we had our grass mowed. I never saw that big rattlesnake. Like, if I’m right here to the corner there [gesture], it laid there that long. When I saw that metal coffee can, I looked over there. It didn’t start rattling till I walked that way. That was it – I couldn’t do nothing. I stopped where I was walking. Its head was right here where I was standing, and its tongue was touching me without stopping. His head was this big [gesture]. Boy, it was no different from what they call Lone Ranger ka-ni-l. That’s what it was like, right here. I was watching it, thinking, “What am I going to do? I can’t do anything.” They were just straight up hard like this [gesture], and he was rattling loud. My wife came out. She said, “What is that?” I didn’t answer her. I was just waiting. I thought, “As soon as it moves, I’m going to pull my leg.” It just stayed like that, and when it backed off and got ready, that’s when I moved. It was like this: I saw the inside of its mouth, but it missed me. Boys, as I was standing there, I fell further from jumping right there. Soon as I hit, I got back up. Its head was like this [gesture] and it was doing this [gesture]. This was a close one. Gah-lee, it really was close. It almost got me in the open. I grew up on the mountain hunting, but I never saw a snake before. Just right there at my house, a big one almost jumped on my back, yeah. I had a bow then, that I’d had for a long time. I had that bow and arrow since the year of ’58. It had iron tips on there. I told them boys to go get that for me. Right there where my house is, when you come up to my house, I was standing over here where the good part ends. You could see it laying there from there. They brought a bow to me. They had a little crossbow, and the boys brought that to me. I told them, “This won’t do anything to it. It’ll probably just make it itch, if you stick it with this,” I told them. “Go get me that big bow.” They went and got it, and three arrows. I drawed back from there. I wasn’t going to get close again. I shot, and the arrow went above it. Then another and same thing – they were sticking like this [gesture]. They were touching each other. And the third time, I lowered it. I pulled back and shot. It was no different than hitting hard on a board, that’s what it sounded like. It hit, and his rattlers just went down. It headed towards Archie’s house. When that snake moved it stayed like this [gesture]. It stayed like that forever. If you were standing over there [gesture], you would think it was a stick sticking out of the ground. That’s how it was. That wood has been laying there for a long time. There’s a big ta-li (Pin Oak tree) by my house. There’s a strong stick laying there. It’s about this big [gesture]. It’s bowed like this [gesture]. I was standing there, and I thought, “Boy, it’s laying there!” I went and got it. It was still like that. I got behind it and I told it, “If you didn’t do that, I wouldn’t have done this to you.” I told it, “I would have let you go, but not now.” I hit it on the neck.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: And you had already stuck it?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, and the arrow went right through it, and it was stuck in the ground. That’s how it happened. And then I told it, “If you’re just going to lay there, I’ll come back in four days and check on you.” Somebody came over, and when he got out, he looked around, and just right quick, he said, “Is that a snake laying over there?” He saw it real quick. After four days, me and the oldest boy measured the snake. It was 13 and a half feet long, when we measured it. By gosh, it was this long [gesture]. Boy, that snake was big, boys. Its body was this big [gesture].

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How many of those [rattles] did it have?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: 39, and they were this big, on the tail end. They were this tall [gesture]. It rattled them loud.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Bobby, have you heard them saying that the snake swallowed a heart? Have you heard that before?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: I was telling him that. I wonder why they were doing that. Was someone really doing that when they lived a long time ago?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: I don’t know about that. I would say to no to caught a disease.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: I’ve heard one. I heard it twice, someone saying that. I don’t know if it’s true. I don’t know if somebody really did do that. But you don’t know what people did when they lived a long time ago.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Them Cherokees, yeah. They knew some stuff. They were really smart. I think about them sometimes. And compared to what we know, that’s what worries me sometimes. How can that happen? I was thinking I came a long ways. How did they know it could happen like that? I tell our people when we talk, “That’s how much they watched what was going on in the world. They were watching what was going on, and what the signs were. That’s how they knew this.”

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: And then when you said that, they didn’t have no television back then. That animal that lives in the woods, how it found its food and what it did – seeing that was teaching them something.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, that was carrying on. I tell them, the kids that we raised, “If y’all pay attention, y’all can realize how the wind is blowing, how it gets cloudy, and how the birds sound. Or if y’all watch how the animals in the woods do, y’all can learn a lot.”

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How do you say what you was saying in English? A-ya-ta-ne-ga.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: In English it would be like ‘it follows’. Yeah, it follows. Yeah, whatever they experienced, what they knew, what they were watching, it was followed by wisdom and knowledge and understanding.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They was following that?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, they was following it, and they was right. They knew this. The other day, two weeks ago, our oldest daughter that we raised, and her husband, they have ducks. They bought three of them somewhere, back in March, and two baby chickens. They have them penned up on the other side. They were over there, and the three of us were sitting there. Then a dla-ga (blue jay) started hollering where they was at.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: What is that dla-ga?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Blue jay. I looked over there, and they were throwing rocks. Then her husband said, “Hey, don’t! It’s telling y’all there’s a snake there somewhere.” They weren’t hearing no more, and that girl left. She came over and said, “What did you say?” “Them birds are telling y’all there’s a snake there somewhere. Go over there,” and then she took off. It wasn’t too long before they said, “Look at what they’re carrying!” They were carrying a snake, and it was this big [gesture].

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: A rattlesnake?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: No, it was part rattlesnake, and this one’s husband looked it up on his phone. He’s smart at doing something with a phone. This is the same if you say it in English – it’s a cross-breed. “They are doing the same,” he said. “It’s a cottonmouth and a chicken snake.” What they had laying there was the same as in the picture. The one they killed had a big head. That’s what the snakes are doing, Michael, yeah. Different snakes are coming together. It wasn’t like that before.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Copperhead didn’t get very big either. A long time ago, it would be just this long [gesture]. Now they seem bigger.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: No. Boy, they would say, that was big, if a copperhead was that long. That’s how it is, and then again, that’s how much I paid attention to the elders talking about it. Boys, I grew up around elders. I never was around kids, maybe just a little while. I was always in the middle of them, doing something and asking for things to do. That’s how I grew up. And what I was saying, Charlie, towards where we lived, it used to be a lot of woods. Where the fields used to be is where they used to plow. We used to grow food there. Most of them and all of us were working there, plowing. When it was time to pull out potatoes, and everything else. They were getting the same amount of what they grew, that’s how it was then. I tell them when we got done planting, one of the old men, Charlie, they would pray. Yeah, they would pray.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: After they got done planting.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: When they got done planting, yeah. They were letting God know they had planted seeds. Now we are done with what we are suppose to do. Now just multiply it. “If it is Your will, we would appreciate it if You would multiply it.” And this is how it was when all of the food grew. And when they started pulling out the potatoes, they had a box. They were putting in the best that grew in there, and they would say, “This is our offering to the Creator.” And they would just put it by the garden. They would pick the best ones. There was some meaning to that, that you had to give an offering.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It’s written in the Bible that the high priest was suppose to bring the best thing they had. They had to offer it.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: They offered it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They must have gotten it from there.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: They must have gotten it from there, yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Like sheep. He had to offer the best sheep he had.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, he had to offer it. Yeah, that’s how it was, it was really… You know, it was really hard for the prices of things, but boys, it was good. Whoever it was, you knew it was family or even if it wasn’t your cousin, everybody was family. If you say it in English, everybody was family that I knew of. And this, when someone dies or died, people cried then. Nobody don’t cry now. That’s what I tell my kids. They’ll just be laughing somewhere and joking around. It wasn’t like that back then. Somebody somewhere might be sitting crying. Three of them be sitting somewhere crying. Back then, when I was growing up, it was four days. After the fourth day was over, that’s when they would say they left us. Yeah, they weren’t going to bury them the next day. Love it was, ’cause they loved this person is the reason why they were going through this. And the family that was left, people weren’t leaving. A month, two months later, some of them were still there helping them out. Then the ones that lived got sick. There were some medicine men who lived near. It was their job to help them get strong and be OK, man or woman. No, it wasn’t like how it is now. I tell them, “If y’all can see it, we’re in poor shape, you know. We’re in poor shape.”

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: And it goes back to that. Our God offered His best and only son. He didn’t have sin in him. He offered the best one.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Offered the best he had. Yes, Charlie, that’s how it really is. That’s how it was, and now they would just be laughing. Nobody… nowadays, somebody would be sitting somewhere thinking about something. And then again, this thing hurt people that I know of. You know how we are living, we don’t visit one another. You know that we don’t visit each other. OK, a long time ago, people used to visit each other till late at night, sitting around talking about stuff, then people go home. It’s gotten this far. Family don’t talk to each other anymore that I know of. All the time I see them do it. I don’t understand it. I don’t know if they say two words to each other when they talk.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: That’s what’s taking over.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: That’s what’s taking over that I know of. That’s sad.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Some of them that’s sitting over there, like we are, that’s how close they sit, and that’s how they used to talk.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s it. That’s what I noticed.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They’re supposed to do what we’re doing, talk, but they’re still using those (phones).

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: This really ain’t no good. But this has been said: it’s going to come to a time. Y’all be careful. A big white snake is going to swallow y’all. They were talking about the government. It all came down to that big snake. They called the government a snake. But boys, this is how it was suppose to be, that’s what I tell people, this is how it was suppose to be. We can’t do nothing about it. The government is trying to have peace all over the world, but it’s not going to happen, it’s not, no. The peace has already gone, Michael. The groups in the world are not peaceful enough to make it right and to heal what’s going on in the world. I tell them that’s the reason why God gave us knowledge, and we all see it. I tell them we’re all going to see something.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: There ain’t no love.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: There ain’t no love.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: If it ain’t for that, we wouldn’t see peace.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: No peace, that’s the truth.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Bob, when you were a boy growing up, we had to draw water, too. It was being used. You weren’t going to go to the store ’cause you didn’t have any money. Would you like to go back and live how it was?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, I would want to, and that’s what I tell them. What we’re talking about right here, boys, the ones that are coming behind us, they are going to acknowledge the same thing, but it’s going to be harder. The same thing is going to happen again, from what I see and how it’s going in the world and what we went through. I tell people, from what I acknowledged and what I see, we’re not going this way [gesture], we’re going this way [gesture]. Whatever happened is going to happen again. That’s what’s clear. I tell people there’s not that much time left, and that’s what’s going to happen. Right there is where we’re going to acknowledge pain, if I’m still alive. If you say it in English, something that has never happened before is going to happen now. You know what’s it’s going to come to. What you said, Michael, when you were drawing water? In the year 1960, all of the water ran out. It got dry – no water, no rain, and both of those creeks went dry. There were spots that had water, and where I was telling y’all where we lived, that well went dry, too. And my uncle, his name was E-li-gi, his young son and my late dad had no water. He wasn’t able to get any drinking water anywhere. They had a chain that they were using in the well, raising them up or we was raising them up. When that happened, they cut a branch off about this big [gesture]. They wrapped the chain around it, and then my dad and the young boy went down the well. They had a light they call flashlight, and where the water went dry, the water was just two feet deep. Somebody missed it by that much when they dug the well. They were pouring them down there, and we were all standing outside, all the people that lived there. They were pouring water in, we was pouring water in them, and when we got all of them barrels filled up, they would come back up. This is what happened one time. They used to call the young man ‘boy’. My late dad spoke and we was standing above. He said, “Boy, do you hear it?” “Yeah, what was it?” My dad said, “I don’t know. I’ve never heard anything like that before,” he told him. “Let’s hurry up and fill these up.” They said, “There’s something coming.” On the south side from where they were standing, there was a big cliff, a big one, and right there was water, just right there. And we heard it, too. My dad said, “It sounds no different from how a bull sounds.” Everybody who was standing above, we all heard it. He said, “Boy, hurry up, it sounds like it’s really close.” To me, it sounded like how a bull frog sounds, but it was big. Like when a cow is mad, that was it. We all heard it. They came back up, and they didn’t go back in the second time. They barely found some water across the railroad tracks in Yv-wa-gv-ni’s field. There was a well by the creek. They found some water there, so we were drawing water from there. Yes, they found out something like that right there.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did they see it?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: No, they didn’t see it. Boys, this right here, about 20 years ago that crossing by where U-lo-gi-lv used to live, we saw a big lizard right there, a big one. Its head was this big [gesture]. We used to take all of my kids there in the evening. They would play around when they were growing up. They would play in the water and when we got ready to leave to go home, when we got there we crossed the creek. We faced the other way, and I turned our ride around. When I got in, I thought I’m going smoke. Right then, they were told, “Come, let’s go home,” right when I lit the cigarette. And right here is the mirror, what they call rear-view mirror. When I done this I saw it. It came up just this much [gesture]. I turned around real fast, and Tammy was standing there. She said, “What is it? Did you see something?” I told her, “Yeah, I’m not going to lie to you, I saw a big lizard.” She said, “Where?” I said, “Just right behind there, about 20 feet behind there. Be quiet, kids.” They were being loud. And right there on the grass, where whatever grew, it moved slow. I was staring at it. I was turned around. It came up, just its head came up. Boy, it took off! Its claws were this long [gesture]. They were black. If the body is here [gesture], if the head’s right here [gesture], and if the tail is here [gesture], that’s where it began. That’s how big the lizard was. Its back was this tall [gesture]. It was running far down the creek. We were listening to the sticks breaking. I was telling Rainwater that, and he said, “There ain’t no telling what it is.” Where it came from, there’s a lot of cliffs. That can really happen, too. Yeah, we saw that kind. And my brother Waite, on this side of Marble City, on the north side, somebody had a chicken farm. He was working there about eight years ago or maybe 10, and he said he saw a big coyote, not one of them small ones. He came over. He said, “Boy,” when he came over to my house, “I’ve never seen a coyote that big.” I said, “Was it pretty big?” He said, “Bob, it was as tall as a cow.” I looked at him and said, “Waite, are you feeling OK?” He started laughing, and he said, “Boy, Bob, it was real.” He said, “Right then, I told the owner of the chickens that I saw that big of a coyote. I guess around one o’clock, four men came inside. I was standing there feeding the chickens. The owner pointed at me and two of them came towards me,” he said. “They walked up to me, and one said, ‘Did you see a big coyote?’ ‘Yeah.’ ‘When?’ ‘This morning. When I got on the road, it was standing by the big field.’ ‘And it was big as a cow?’” He said he told them it was as big as a cow, and it was that tall. He said the head was this big [gesture]. He said he was watching it, thinking, “Is there something wrong with me?” He said, “I was thinking that this was going to happen someday.” One said, ‘Where do y’all throw them chickens?’ He said over there. He told him, ‘Let’s go over there.’ He said they got in the pick-up with the dead chickens, and he said, “There’s something wrong.” That’s what I was thinking. I thought about it a few times – when is something like that going to happen? There was something strong in the chicken feed to help them grow. He said, ‘You haven’t seen anything eating it, like a dog or chicken?’ He said he told him a lizard and then a bobcat, and coyotes and cats. He said the next day, they brought a big furnace and they put inside. He said that guy said, “You don’t know how big things grow around here.”

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That’s what was making it grow.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, he said that was what was making him grow.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: That’s true, what y’all are saying. When I was working at the poultry [farm], a chicken would be this big [gesture], and they would bring it into the chicken house. It would be that big, and in 35 or 36 days, that chicken would be this big [gesture], like what you’re saying.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Too fast, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Yeah, they still have that to make them grow when something eats it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Them cows, they call it antibiotics. I don’t if it’s the same antibiotics we know. They put them in here and that’s what makes them grow fast. I don’t how much they pay for it.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: From a person’s own smartness, I’m just going to say, it’s getting dangerous.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, we’re all going to be gone, just because of a person’s own smartness.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: How about them robots? You can say that, ain’t it, them making robots like a real person?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: It’s really sad what happened to our stepdaughter’s husband. They found cancer starting in his colon. That kind done surgery on him, and they almost did something to him in Tulsa.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: They gave him some kind of medicine, or what?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: No, they done surgery on him like the kind you’re saying – a robot. Where they had measured to cut it off, it shorten it by three inches. They said now they can’t fix it. He’s got [gesture] that hanging on him.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Colostomy bag. I don’t know if I said that right.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, that kind.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Where he uses the bathroom.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah. That’s how much that thing you’re saying caused it. That’s how much it cut it, they said. They couldn’t attach it back together. Look at what they’re doing to us. It’s just like what I said a while ago. When they came in when we were talking, they were putting us down forever, just us, too. You know us five? You know five of us. Us Indians got put under the law. They made us to where we can do nothing about it. And them, the other ones, they live like they can do whatever they want to do. Cheyenne, Arapaho, all of them, but not us. We’re put inside the law forever. We can’t get out of it, not ever. That’s what I think about. I wonder why they did that. You know the BIA? Yeah. Have they not acknowledged it? Boy, I think they should have acknowledged it, the ones that know the books. No, I would say they haven’t acknowledged it. If a person knows something about the books, they have wisdom. Yeah, they know something. And the ones that don’t know the books, they don’t know anything. Just like me, boys, I can’t tell y’all anything that y’all know. Y’all can tell me ’cause I don’t know anything. Do y’all understand what I’m saying?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, I don’t know anything that y’all know yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It’s the same, we don’t know what you know.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s the truth. Do you know what I acknowledged here recently? A coyote, a coyote that lives in the woods, and us Indians, that’s how I saw myself, as I saw us Indians, it’s the same as the coyotes. The coyotes don’t have a place to go anymore. Nowhere. That’s how far the law got. It is measured just how far it can go, and where it’s measured, it’s getting smaller. Charlie, that’s what’s going to happen to us. That’s what’s going to happen to the ones coming behind us when we’re not alive. That’s where this is headed.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: The children coming.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, the children coming, they are going to see it. It’s going to be very sad. I tell them it’s very sad, it’ll make you cry. I tell them that’s how sad it’s going to get, from what I see. Something that’s never happened before is going to happen. A person that has never been examined before is going to get examined. I tell people that’s where we’re all headed. If you say it in English, we’re going to be tested like men have never been, you know, tested of their faith in the time of man. Our faith is going to get looked at that, is where we are headed. I tell people to pray, and let go of the world. The world is nothing. Boys, just like when I was young, I used to think it was awesome when I was able to go places. I picked the most baddest place. My parents were telling me that, too. Yeah, that’s what I did.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: You mentioned that a while ago, a long time ago, people depended on God and they also depended on their jobs. On those two. With their sweat, they looked for stuff – fish, garden, looked for wood. They put effort into it, and when they found it, they thanked God for it. And now I don’t know what people depend on. I guess just on a person’s smartness. A person ain’t smart enough to get you through the hard times.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Huh-uh, he’s not smart enough. Michael, what you just said. The one who raised me the one we called dad, right there where I’m telling y’all, where Wa-ne used to live, there’s a mountain there. It’s rocky and we came over that Nv-ya-tsu–su-go, y’all know where that’s at – Bunch, Hanging Rock where that rock is. Nv-ya-tsu-su-go, where the rocks broke off.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Oh, yeah, that’s what it’s called.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Right there, Charlie, we would come over. It’s rocky here, rattlesnakes and other snakes live here. He had a little flashlight; it was dim and we had that. We were sitting there, he was fishing with a cane pole, and boy, he was catching them, he really was catching them. And then we would go back at midnight. We were making it through OK. But like what you said, Michael, there were people that prayed. Just the other day, I told them boys, I told my young boys that I raised where I came from, my parents. “Your grandmas and your grandpas went through some really scary stuff. They had given up on their lives. They were looking for some food for us to eat and for us to have it better,” I said. “Where are we doing that now?” Like what you’re saying, people are looking at their wisdom and when they can’t make it, everybody is going to fight. Yeah, that’s how far we’ve gotten. A person can get mad and angry real fast, and do something. I tell them it’s not supposed to be like that, just forget about it. I tell them we’re not always going to live, and we can’t win anyway. Yeah, it’s better to be nice, to be honest. That’s how it was when they were looking for blackberry and blueberry and water. I forgot this, boys. One day, they pull potatoes out and they say they won’t go bad in the month of July, but boys, I forgot this and another one I forgot, too, Charlie. One day in July, the fish – any kind of fish – goes up stream, one day a year.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: I’ve heard of what you’re saying.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: That one day?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It goes up the creek?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Creek, yeah. That creek in Greasy and Sallisaw, and where they meet, we would go there. And they had thin burlap sacks and gigs. My grandpa would tell his young boys, my dad, let’s sit right here somewhere. I was sitting there thinking, “When are we going to go fishing?” It was kind of bothering me that we weren’t doing anything. “Grandpa, when are we going to fish?” “Wait just a little bit. They’ll be here in a minute.” It’s where the water shifts is where I’m talking about. It’s just this deep [gesture]. He would say, “Now, here they come.” I hear them making the water splash going up. “Now, go catch them and throw them outside.” I would run around. I was throwing any kind of fish outside, and the men and young men now with gigs. We were killing a lot of fish. Then we would go home and on the way back somewhere, on Ya-wi-gu-nu’s property, they would fix them for the women to cook when we got back. That’s how it was, yes that’s how it was. Boys, that was good.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s what I was saying to you a while ago. Would you want to go back and live then and see people again and cook outside and eat?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Or just to talk?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, just to talk.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: They used to be joking around back then.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: They were funny, ain’t it? There wasn’t anybody not laughing back then, laughing at things. What I was saying, the late A-tsa-di Sambo Andrew Glass and they had those hand carts by our house. There’s a big house in the field – that’s where we lived. They were talking about A-tsa-di, and it was Sambo. They were saying, “When he comes back, we’re going to plow.” Boy, I was in a hurry for A-tsa-di to come back. I never did ask them where he was.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Was that their dad or what?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: No it was…

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: They were brothers?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: The late Sambo?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, they were.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: That was Andrew.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, that was his name in English.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Sambo was Andrew’s name?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, his name was Andrew. I was thinking, “Boy, I wish A-tsa-di would hurry up and come back,” not knowing who he was. I was hungry. They were saying, “We’re going to plow when he gets here.” He was in the Army. They’d been talking about it for a long time. Then later on, my late dad said, “Son, let’s go to the store,” he said. “Let’s go look for salt and grease.”

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: In Bunch?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, in Bunch. And that’s where they had those hand carts, yeah. He said, “Son, can you help me put this on there? We’ll ride this, boy.” I was scared. I was thinking, “Boy, a train is going to catch us somewhere.” So we put it on there, and there was a piece of metal sticking out here that was the brake, and he sat on that side, and he said, “You have to do it like this.” He helped me, and it was me now.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: You were bending over?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, I was bending over now, towards Bunch. We made it all the way to Bunch, then we took it off again. We went that way – he went and got it. On our way back, there was a room on this side and it was the post office for Bunch back then. He turned back around. He said, “There might be mail in there.” And there was really mail, and it was from A-tsa-di. He opened it when we was on the railroad, and he said, “Son, A-tsa-di said he was going to be back on Wednesday, if he’s in the train. Right there where the hill, the big hill is, starting from there all the way to the bridge, before it gets there, it’s going to blow its horn seven times.” Boy, I don’t know if I ran around the hand cart four times, being happy. Yeah, we put it back on there. And now I just bent over a few times – it was all downhill there. Now I was just standing there holding on. When we got there, I took off running. After we got it off, I went and told my late mom, “My dad is saying A-tsa-di is going to be coming back.” Boy, I was awake till midnight thinking about A-tsa-di. I was in a hurry for him to come back. “We’re going to plow when I get back where he has it.” He’s going to buy horses and a tiller where it’s at. Then my dad went to Di-ga-l-s-gi and told people and to his parents Sambo’s, all of the people came over. They were all sitting around and I was walking around. I was thinking, “I hope that train blows its horn,” and then I heard it. It was blowing its horn from Stilwell. Then I sat down, thinking, “I don’t know if I was saying ‘Let that train blow its horn.’” And it really came through Bunch crossing blowing its horn. Boy, I was thinking, I wish it would blow its horn when it gets there. When it got there by Maxwell Mountain, it blew its horn long. I was listening to it when he let go. It blew another long one, and it was coming. And when it blew the third time, I thought, “He’s in there,” and then I started running around again fast. And right there where that road goes towards where Dave used to live, and somewhere around there at the bridge, the train started slowing down and braking. Then everybody stood up and went towards the railroad where the gate is. The train stopped there. That was him, he was wearing Army clothes, and they got two blue-tick hound dogs out. He lived overseas and came to New York, and then this way.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Towards Bunch.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Towards Bunch. It started the next morning. The late Jim Harris took him to town around evening. I heard some chains, and we were down by the creek, and I kept looking down the road. I saw something – its ears were just like this [gesture]. They were coming. He bought two side-by-side, the little ones. They had ducks and chickens and two milk cows on a leash and a tiller. It started right then. They didn’t wait till the morning. When they hooked up the horses and hooked up the tiller, it started right then. It was probably around 1:30 in the morning. Right where Sambo lived, they lived by the field, it’s all woods now. There are trees this big [gesture] there. From there, there weren’t any bushes anywhere then. They plowed right there. They would let me take over. It was stretching my legs around and I was getting after it. We grew a lot of stuff there. That’s what I was saying to them boys that live at home, or people, even young men, or just whoever I talk to. I told them I worked even harder cause I appreciated it. Now you know where the good is. When the food is made and when they cook it and when you eat, I tell them that’s what I think about. That’s where all the good is, where you made an effort. Yeah, you know, yourself, yeah. That’s how it was. Right there, where it’s a forest, boys, it wasn’t like that a long time ago when I was growing up. On the railroad side was the only fence up and on this side was a forest. There were no bushes nowhere. That’s what I was telling them. Where we live and where S-u-di used to live, they were talking over there, and we were all seeing each other. And on the Willson side, on the bluff, that’s how it was, Charlie. There weren’t any bushes anywhere. And now it’s thicket, real thicket. Why is it?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: ’Cause nobody don’t go there anymore, that’s why it’s so thicket and bushy.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: When they put the fence up. Yeah, boys, that’s how it is. Yes, things are happening more. It’s filling up. I tell people it’s not going to be much longer. Now we’re really going to experience it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Let me ask you this. The medicine that lives in the woods, is it running out?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: That again, I experienced it. Where the White people plowed, that’s where it’s growing. You used to find it on the side of the road, but now you can’t. All the mowers have caused it all to go away. Now we don’t have enough land to go look for the medicine. It’s all on that side. Some of it is disappearing that I know of. I know one kind of medicine for jaundice. They call it black it’s medicine for the blood veins that is hard to find now. That’s some real medicine boys this black. It will heal a person.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What’s wrong with a person? When they have that black, what’s wrong with them?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: It makes them lazy or sleepy. And if you don’t heal them, later in time it will make them hallucinate. Like if something is sitting there, I can picture it like if it’s over there, and you know if it’s overpowering him if he looks there. It might move somewhere and it might move back quick, and if a person comes to that, they are real sick. This is the medicine right here for the veins, and the White doctors can’t help you, I know it. They’ll send you somewhere and say you’re crazy. Yeah that’s how it is. We’re made to heal people. Yeah, I know three of them that’s happened to them in there, in somewhere. They won’t never heal them. They give them pills, it just makes them worse. I watch them, I watch everything that’s wrong with us. And I tell people again, how come y’all don’t obey? We have our own medicine. Yeah, you can’t do nothing. All you can do is tell them. If they do want to do it, it’s their own decision.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Now on the White man’s property, they’re being stingy with their land. They are not allowing anybody to go get something that’s growing there.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s why. Just like wild turkey and deer, they’re in there. Yeah, it’s the same with them.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I have diabetes. What’s the medicine when you have diabetes?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: There’s a few that were left to me. Cane pole. The cane pole you fish with, hard-boil the root. And the winter huckleberry boiled hard. Have y’all seen it, boys? It lives by the water, and its buds are like Johnson grass, but it’s not it. It grows just a little bit. From morning till noon, the buds have like spit on them. All of the buds from the stem, those four roots, and scratched it four times, and boil it. That’s what I was told. And another one, qua-lo-ga, that one, too, the sour one. They said that one, too.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Is it like the berry kind?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, the berry kind.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What do you do to that?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Just put it in water. Put it in water.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You don’t boil it?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: No, you don’t boil it, you just put it in water. If you put it in water today, it will be done tomorrow. It’s like sour, you will know how it is. And cherry tree branches are just now growing in the summer. They are reconnecting every year. You can tell where they reconnect, where they’ve broken off. Get this many of them, about this big [gesture], and wrap a white cloth around it. Put seven of the qua-lo-ga in a gallon of water. A person ain’t supposed to eat a fried egg, no beans, no onion, and no pickles. It is forbidden – it won’t heal them, I was told.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: While they are using that?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, while they are using that. But after they get better, I was told whatever they eat first, they’ll know if they still have it. I was told if they eat a fried egg, and if the disease is still in the blood vein, it will make them really sick. One more gallon, not hot. This medicine is pretty good, that’s what I was told. I was told if you drink too much of it, your blood pressure might go down, if a person’s sugar is getting low, yeah. I was told just one gallon. If they drink one gallon, they’re not suppose to drink it again the second time. And if a person has high blood pressure, what I was told, in English they call it blood root, I’ve heard that that’s it. That, boys, when I was growing up, they used that kind to help the blood. Not too much of the root – it might do something to you if you drink too much of it. If someone had a toothache, that’s what they used. I was thinking about it. About five years ago, I saw a bush of that, and I took the root. I just kept it. I was sitting at home, and I thought about that. I wondered how… ’cause you couldn’t ask anything when I was growing up. If they wanted you to know, they would tell you, and if they didn’t tell, then you didn’t ask. That’s how the elders were. Yeah, nowadays, the kids will be going around saying, “What is it? What is it?” This root, if you break it, will bleed like blood. And I did that to this. I thought about what it was like, and there was nothing wrong with it. I was sitting there, and it was like my lip started to swell up. I thought, “What’s wrong?” I was touching it, and then my tongue started doing the same thing. Gah-lee, it seemed like my tongue was this thick [gesture]. I got up and went in the house. I went in and I looked at my tongue in the mirror, and my mouth was the same. That will make you really numb. It’ll make you numb, it will make you really numb, yeah. This one person, a White person, about two weeks ago this person had a toothache and couldn’t do anything ’cause he didn’t have insurance. He was crying around, and I told him, “I know some medicine. If you want to you can try it. It’s up to you.” I went and looked for some, and just a little while later, he was laughing around, yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did you just rub it on there for him?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, just like I’m saying, I told him, “Put a little bit on the Q-tip and put it on where it’s hurting.” Yeah, it got better after that. Yeah, there’s also words of medicine you can say for a toothache. That, boys, is what I was saying. You know, I was thinking, “How can that happen?” But it was working. For a long time, I wondered how. I finally remembered that it was faith. Yeah, faith. Faith, for real.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: If the person who’s using it don’t have faith, it’s not going to help them.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: No, it won’t help them if they don’t have faith. That’s what I say to them. You got to have faith and believe, and if you don’t, it won’t help you. That’s how it is. There is medicine to help us. When I was growing up, my grandpas took me in the woods, and that’s where they were teaching me what kind of roots, and telling me, “This is how you do it.” Yeah. And if a person is dizzy, they’re not supposed to eat green beans. Like, if a person gets dizzy – there were some people that got dizzy, and I was told they’re not supposed to eat green beans. Or if a person has had a stroke, they said they’re not supposed to eat wild bean vine.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Is that bean vine?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, v-ya-a-ti, bean vine. It’s not good. It might…

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Can you still find it down that way?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, there is still some. Yeah, there is still some, Michael. A-du-gi is out, too. I’ve been watching that a-du-gi growing up. That’s when I’m doing good. I don’t know, it might be tomorrow that I’ll cook a-du-gi. They’ve never eaten that before, those who live at my house. I’m going to cook that. Gah-lee, it’s good.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I’ve ate it before.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: You ate it before?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: It tastes good. I like to eat it. It’s good to eat. Michael, it tastes good. Another thing is that cotsuni.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I don’t like that.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: You don’t like that? Some people tell me they don’t like that. I like cotsuni with eggs in it, yeah. And another one, cotsuni and that watercress, if you mix them up and make as one, I think that tastes good, too.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Corn bread.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Corn bread. Boy, and brown beans and about this much [gesture] backed up grease. Yeah, boys, that is good to eat.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How about what you were telling us a while ago? The big leg – tell us that so we can record it.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Alright, boys, this is true. Some think it’s not, but I believe it’s true, and it lives. A lot of people will doubt you, y’all know. Just like what you would say in English: dinosaurs. Some people, a lot of them, don’t believe in that. They lived a long time ago. They really lived. There were some big people alive, about 20 feet tall, long time ago. And this Bigfoot, you know I think about something like that. How come only some people see it? Not everybody sees it. I think just like, you know, if you say it in English, it’s kind of like a spirit to me. And it’s really smart to hide. And here, around midnight, right there where Roger Vann lived, the late U-s-qua-ti used to live there. There was a house there, and when U-s-qua-ti passed away, they was old, and then Parker Johnson and Sallie rented it. They lived there. And I would come from where we lived, and they would watch TV. I would go watch it there, and when it was over – the boys Leon Rosin and James called it Gunsmoke. When that was over, I would walk home. It was then that one time at night, something walked with me. It walked with me for about a mile. Really, we walked that far, and I was using a lighter for a light, but [I could see] nothing. What I thought, Charlie, what I experienced, it hit me like this [gesture], like this. It didn’t touch me. I was wearing what they call a short-sleeve t-shirt. It was like I felt something or somebody’s hair. It happened, and it was right there when I got weak. I saw it real quick. It was probably eight feet tall. That’s what I was saying. I reached out, and its face was still right here. And it didn’t look like what they call the man-eater, or what they call a chimpanzee in English. It wasn’t like that. The face looked different. I can picture it for y’all. It looked like a human’s face to me. Not like our faces, but different. It looked like a human’s face. I know when I saw it, and its hair. Its hair was long. It had hair all over it. It didn’t have hair on its face, but its hair was long. That’s how that thing was. “Huh!” is all I said. I was about to give up – it started right there. It probably thought I was dancing for it. I was barely standing.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: It made your feet itch?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Boy, it sure did, but I thought I better not run. I thought, “If it’s going to get me, it’s going to get me. I can’t outrun it, anyway.” That’s how that thing happened. That’s how close I saw that thing they talk about. This was probably about over 50 years ago that I saw what I’m telling y’all. It’s probably been three, no, five years ago, I believe, that where we live now, that bluff, one of those went by there. The dogs were barking at something. They weren’t even going up the hill. I was listening, and it was clear the branches were breaking sometimes. I got off the porch and got on this side, right there where that snake was coming. It went downhill there on the west side. It did that for a while. Maybe two months went by. One time I thought, “I’m going to check if that thing is coming back by.” I sat on the porch all night long waiting for it. It was 4:30 when it went back that way. Charlie, it might be living towards the pines, and then again, it might be towards where they call Christie Hollow. That’s where they saw it, at Christie Hollow. And where Sambo lives and Sauce’s nieces and nephews live, they seen it there, too, and some turkey hunters. They went around where Tom Starr used to live. It was during the day when they seen it there crossing. Yeah, it’s true. But I believe it ain’t just one. People believe it’s just one. There ain’t no telling how many of them are around. And now it’s making a man is ga-nu-da-ti and everything that lives in the woods is going to come out, even snakes.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They’re running out of places to live.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, they’re running out of places to live. I tell people, “You’ve got to watch yourself. You don’t really know what’s going to come around.”

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Is that just the one time you seen it?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, I just saw it one time. I heard something there at Pine Hollow [by] Wolf Mountain. Something was hollering real bad and loud. I don’t know what it was – we never saw it. And another one by the house, towards the creek. We go to the creek by the house. We go cut grass there. You can get real close to the creek. It’s a nice place to be. It was there where something was hollering. It was like something got a hold of an adult pig, like how they squeal. That’s how it sounded, and when it got done doing that, it would growl. It was hollering four times. It would get quiet for about four minutes. Me and one of our young boys we raised were standing outside, listening to it. Four minutes after it hollered four times, it hollered in Maxwell Mountain somewhere, and the second time you could barely hear it in Bunch. It was probably in Bunch. Then after that, when me and Tammy were at the clinic in Stilwell, them Muskrats from Bell were there. They were telling me that at the pow-wow grounds, there by the creek, something went by there. They told me it sounded the same. I don’t know, about three nights or four nights going back towards Marble City, something went by there for a while, Charlie. I don’t know what it was, but that’s how it was. It was hollering loud. People heard it, they were hearing it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How about when they say he beats up on a tree? Have you heard that?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Here a while back, I was hearing something like what I’m saying. Where Sambo used to live, I was hearing something like that over there, and it was at night. I thought, “Who’s using an axe?” That’s where it ended. I didn’t think anything more about it. I’ve heard something like that before, like someone is hitting something like a barrel or an old tree. Thump, thump. It was towards the bluff when I heard something like that. That’s why I thought someone was using an axe.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I’ve heard that before. You know where Bob Maxie lives?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Towards where the Cherokees have land, that’s where we were trapping pigs. I was sitting there by myself. We put corn out there for when they come over. That’s what I was doing. It was starting to get evening time when it made a noise behind me. It was like a gunshot, but it wasn’t a gun. And it was four times. Man, it was loud. It didn’t bother me at the time. When I got back home, that’s when it bothered me. I thought, “They say that’s what it does.” I have heard it before.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: So you have heard it before?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: But it wasn’t…

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: It wasn’t anything different.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I would have looked around and thought about that real fast, but I didn’t. I just went back to waiting on them pigs.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: That Gerald Pettit seen it, too, by the game refuge going out of the game refuge, going towards Cookson, where that cattle guard is on that straightaway. A long time ago, they used to say there was a building. The building might still be there – it used to be a school. He said he was right there with his sister. They were going to Cookson. Gerald said he was looking around. It was last year, around this time of the month. He said he was looking around, and where you could see good, he said, “I don’t know if there was ever a road there,” he said. “It was sitting there,” he said. “It was sitting on the ground,” he said. “It had a bunch of hair on it.” He said he told his sister, “Look! Stop!” That thing they see is sitting over there. “She stopped, and we backed up. I seen it was running away. It had already run pretty far.” He was saying, “I saw that kind over there, yeah. Just like the little people.”

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That’s what I was going to ask you.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: A lot of people don’t believe those little people are real. Yeah, they are real. I’ve seen seven of them coming up. I’ve seen three of them this tall [gesture]. Two old men and an old lady. These were really old. Right there where the pow-wow is, either way you go, if you go through Salem, it goes up the hill where the gravel road meets. Right there where I was telling y’all where Tsu-da-e-ga lived, I really went with him. I spent the night with them, and then the next morning – there’s a spring just below there. He said, “Can you go get some water?” I went down there, and past halfway there, I heard somebody talking. I couldn’t make out which way it was. Then I stopped. After a little while, it seemed like it was towards that way [gesture]. Then I saw it, right there at the spring. There was a creek where the spring was, and they were standing there – two old men and an old lady. One of them had a switch, and he was doing this [gesture] to the water. I was watching. There I was, behind a tree. I was barely peeking out. Right when I looked, the old lady just turned around and looked at me. They took off. They disappeared right there while I was watching them. And the other ones, where we call it a swimming hole by the house, these were young. Yeah, I saw three of them. They were this tall [gesture]. The one that was walking last saw me. There was a rock laying here and they went around it. I was watching them sitting on a rock. When they came down, I was watching them looking at them. When they were walking, the one that was walking last saw me. It did this [gesture]. It put its head down. Right when it did that, I jumped off and took off running, and then there was nothing. When I was a little boy, it was this tall [gesture], and it came to visit me. It was just this tall [gesture]. They had those bows that use arrows, and had green clothes on, like those that come on television that have that kind of clothes on. And my mom and dad, I could tell when it was outside, and my mom had a can, a five-gallon can that she put flour in, right there by the window. Where we lived, down the holler towards where Wa-ne used to live, the window opened outward, and then you could close it back from inside. Boy, I push it out and got up there. “I’m not waiting on you!” But I could see its mouth. It was dancing for me. It was dancing and I was watching it. It was jumping, it was hitting its heels like this [gesture], and it was always doing this to me. Then one time, I told my mom and dad that a man was calling me outside, that little man. They said, “Quit saying that right now!” I got spanked real quick. They told me, “There ain’t no man calling you nowhere.” That happened for four days. It was good here and it was grassy there. I kind of got in trouble, ’cause of him I was getting spanked. And I noticed that he came over again. I was getting mad at him. He was calling me, and I did this: I spat at him. I made him mad. His face turned different. He walked around and did this [gesture]. He was stomping his feet like this [gesture]. He was doing this to me with his mouth. He turned around – he was just a little way away and he disappeared. I never saw him again. I’ve seen something just that tall [gesture], yeah. I seen one this tall [gesture]. This one came inside the house, the one we live in right now. Yeah, at midnight we’ve seen that two times in that trailer house we lived in. They saw it then. I didn’t see it, but this last time, probably about five years ago I was watching TV. The fisherman. I kept seeing something by the TV. I thought, “Is something on?” I let the TV go off. I was just staring at that. It appeared there, it knew I saw it, and real quick [gesture]. No more, I never saw it again. They have a trail there. Where A-tsi used to live, the little people had a trail there, too, at Tsu-tsa-I. This is true.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They didn’t say if they saw them?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: My family didn’t.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How about A-tsi?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: He said he heard them talking while they were walking.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They say they will get you lost.

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, they will get you lost. They will really get you lost. There are a lot of things going on in this world we live in, and what we experience, and what we know. And that’s the truth.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Are we just going to finish?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, we’ll just finish.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I asked you what you thought was going to happen to the Cherokee language, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: bobby-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah. Yeah, Charlie, it is going to run out.
